argument_macro_structure.dominant_argument_form: Socratic dialectic is a virtuous, transformative practice because it combines elenchus (refutation) and psychagogia (soul-leading) to produce aporia, which cures dogmatism and reorients desire; its normative power is neither purely intrinsic nor purely extrinsic but emerges from a feedback loop between initial moral openness and the internal mechanics of inquiry.

distinctions_drawn: aporia as failure vs. aporia as generative

objections_raised: Socratic ignorance vs. claim to improve others
dialectic vs. sophistry both use language

summary_of_core_decisions: The text argues that Socratic dialectic is a virtuous, transformative practice because it combines elenchus (refutation) and psychagogia (soul-leading) to produce aporia, which cures dogmatism and reorients desire; its normative power is neither purely intrinsic nor purely extrinsic but emerges from a feedback loop between initial moral openness and the internal mechanics of inquiry.
